question.text: If one root of \(x^2+p x-q^2=0, p\) and \(q\) are real, be less than 2 and other be greater than 2, then

solution.text:
Hint :
\(\alpha < 2\) and \(\beta > 2\) Let, \(\mathrm{p}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{px}-\mathrm{q}^2\) \(\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{p}(2) < 0 \\ & \Rightarrow 2^2+2 p-\mathrm{q}^2 < 0 \\ & \Rightarrow 4+2 p-\mathrm{q}^2 < 0 \end{aligned}\)
